title: Recipe 19 — Rate Limiting and Budgets (three orthogonal limits on one daemon)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Three guardrails that look alike and are not: a rate limit bounds requests per second, a budget bounds tokens per period, and the cost tracker only reports. In production you want all three.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — the committed recipe and starters are never touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env — the gateway needs a Claude credential to actually spend a tenant's budget.

groups.title: Beat 1 · the tenancy the limits key on

beats.label: Type the managed starter
beats.cue: “Recipe 19's prerequisite is tenancy — without it the dimensions collapse and the whole design loses its point. Fifteen lines: one agent, two tenants, and a token budget each.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “Clean. The budget is a first-class spec field, not external policy bolted on at deploy time.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The tenants array survives lowering, ids and budgets exactly as written. The gateway reads this, not the YAML.”

verify.note: prints the IR for target managed, tenants + budgets included

beats.label: Compile the daemon
beats.cue: “The bundle is emitted and the spec registered — that's what the limits attach to. The managed daemon is scaffolding here; recipe 11 is where its boot gets proved.”

verify.note: emits the daemon bundle and registers the spec. Deliberately not --check: a managed daemon binds :3000, and --check scrubs the environment (so PORT cannot be overridden), which means exactly one driver in the suite may boot one — that is recipe 11's.

beats.label: Open the emitted daemon
beats.cue: “JWT verify, tenant rebase, budget accounting, audit chain — the whole enforcement path, as TypeScript you own.”

beats.label: Find the budget gate in the generated code
beats.cue: “The spec's numbers are compiled in as literals, and the accounting backend is a line of the bundle. Pre-flight estimate at the gateway, post-flight update per turn — both live here, not in a doc.”

verify.note: matches createBudgetStore, the per-tenant budget literals from the spec, and the 429 budget_exceeded shed path

beats.label: Type the recipe's rateLimits block
beats.cue: “Three buckets over the (tenant, provider, tool) tuple. Wildcards collapse a dimension — the third one caps Bash at one call a second across the whole deployment.”

beats.label: Parse it back
beats.cue: “Token-bucket, leaky-bucket, token-bucket. Token for human-driven traffic that arrives in bursts; leaky when you sit upstream of a provider that returns 429 on bursts.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const c = Bun.YAML.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("live/rate-limits.yaml", "utf8")); console.log(c.rateLimits.length, "buckets:", c.rateLimits.map((b) => b.algorithm + " " + JSON.stringify(b.keys)).join("  |  "))'

beats.label: Watch back-pressure, not rejection
beats.cue: “A five-per-second bucket, pumped with ten acquires. It does not throw — it makes you wait. That is the difference between a rate limit and a budget.”
beats.command: bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { createRateLimiter } from "@crewhaus/rate-limiter"; const buckets = new Map([["tenant:tenant-a", { kind: "token-bucket", capacity: 5, refillPerSec: 5 }]]); const rl = createRateLimiter({ buckets }); const t0 = Date.now(); for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) await rl.acquire([{ dimension: "tenant", id: "tenant-a" }]); console.log("10 acquires against a 5/s token bucket:", Date.now() - t0, "ms elapsed — back-pressure, not rejection")'

verify.note: ~1000 ms elapsed — the real @crewhaus/rate-limiter out of the bundle --check installed. Takes about a second on purpose; that is the proof

beats.label: Type the recipe's tenant budgets
beats.cue: “Same tenants list, now with periods. Monthly resets on the first at UTC midnight, daily at UTC midnight, and perRun is the right answer for an evaluation pipeline — a fixed budget per run, no carryover.”

beats.label: Parse the periods back
beats.cue: “Two tenants, two different period boundaries, one daemon. Budget exhaustion mid-conversation is a period problem, not a limit problem.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const c = Bun.YAML.parse(require("fs").readFileSync("live/tenant-budgets.yaml", "utf8")); for (const t of c.tenants) console.log(t.id, "→ period", t.budget.period ?? "monthly (default)", "· fields:", Object.keys(t.budget).join(", "))'

verify.note: tenant-a → monthly, tenant-b → daily; each with maxInputTokens/maxOutputTokens/period

groups.title: Beat 5 · drive one tenant's traffic through the gate

beats.label: Pin the JWT secret and tenant root
beats.cue: “At least sixteen characters or the daemon refuses to bind, and tenant storage rebased under live/ so the audit trail stays on camera.”

verify.note: without the secret the daemon mints a one-shot dev one; default tenant root is /tmp/crewhaus-tenants

beats.label: Boot the gateway
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Gateway listening on :3000.” Backgrounded, so this same terminal can drive it.

verify.note: boots with no key; serving a run needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Mint tenant-a's token
beats.cue: “Keyless — HS256 over the secret we just exported into this same terminal. It also proves @crewhaus/gateway-server resolves from the bundle --check installed.”
beats.command: TENANT_A_JWT=$(bun --cwd live/dist -e 'import { signJwt } from "@crewhaus/gateway-server"; console.log(signJwt({ tenant_id: "tenant-a" }, process.env.CREWHAUS_GATEWAY_JWT_SECRET))')

verify.note: local signing, no network, no provider credentials — a 159-char JWT into the shell variable the next beat uses

beats.label: Create a run as tenant-a
beats.cue: [needs-key] “The pre-flight estimate runs before any model call. Drop maxInputTokens to a thousand and this same call answers 429 budget_exceeded instead — the recipe's own way to test the gate.”
beats.command: curl -s -X POST http://localhost:3000/rpc -H "Authorization: Bearer $TENANT_A_JWT" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"protocol":"crewhaus.v1","id":"1","method":"runs.create","params":{"spec":"hello-managed","input":"What is the capital of France?","sessionId":"sess_0123456789abcdef"}}'

verify.note: crewhaus.v1 envelope; the budget gate is enforced before the model call, but a successful answer needs Anthropic credentials

beats.label: Stop the gateway
beats.cue: [needs-key] Job %1 is the daemon the boot beat backgrounded — skip this and the take leaves a process holding :3000.

verify.note: kills the backgrounded daemon from the run-boot beat

groups.title: One more thing · the limiter and the tracker, asserted

beats.label: Run the recipe's Try-it smoke
beats.cue: “Probe 2 is recipe 19's own end-to-end for the limiter, probe 1 for the cost tracker: three model responses priced from the table, summing to a USD total the smoke asserts to the microdollar.”

verify.note: all probes passed — probe 2 asserts back-pressure ≥ 800 ms on a 5 req/s bucket, probe 1 asserts totalUsdMicros 21875. Redirected rather than piped so the exit code is the smoke's own

beats.label: Read the probe log
beats.cue: “Rate limit absorbs the spike, budget enforces the period, cost tracker reports for billing. Three limits, one deployment, none of them substituting for the others.”
